ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are three circles of equal radius arranged horizontally, and the three centers are marked with black dots and are on the same straight line. The visible thick solid arcs on the outside form the boundary of the required figure; the dashed arcs in the middle overlapping part are not the boundary. The left and right circles respectively intersect the middle circle, and the middle circle passes through the centers of the left and right circles. Then reason: The radius of each circle is R. Because the middle circle passes through the centers of the left and right circles, the distance between adjacent centers is R. For two circles whose radii are both R and whose distance between centers is also R, the two centers and either intersection point form an equilateral triangle with side length R, therefore the central angle corresponding to adjacent circles at the intersection points is 120°, while the small arc on the other side corresponds to 120°, and the large arc exposed on the outside is 360° - 120° = 240°. So the left circle contributes a 240° arc, and the right circle also contributes a 240° arc. The exposed arc above the middle circle connects the two upper intersection points, corresponding to a central angle of 60°; the exposed arc below is likewise also 60°. The total central angle is 240° + 240° + 60° + 60° = 600° = 10π/3 radians. The arc length formula is s = Rθ, therefore the perimeter is R · 10π/3 = 10πR/3.

method.method_draft: Directly trace the solid outer boundary. From the image, identify three equal circles in a horizontal row with only the exposed solid arcs forming the shape perimeter; the dashed arcs are not part of the perimeter. From the text, use that all radii are R and the middle circle passes through the centers of the left and right circles, so adjacent circle centers are R apart. For two equal circles of radius R whose centers are R apart, the two centers and either intersection point form an equilateral triangle, giving a 120° angle between the two intersection radii at each adjacent circle. Therefore the exposed arc on the left circle is the major arc of 240°, and the exposed arc on the right circle is also 240°. On the middle circle, the exposed top arc between the two upper intersections is 60°, and the exposed bottom arc is another 60°. Add arc lengths using s=Rθ: total angle = 240°+240°+60°+60°=600°=10π/3 radians, so the perimeter is 10πR/3.
